overlay:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: ONE production head-armor OVERLAY texture for the PLAYER FISH in EVO: Living World, a premium hand-painted 2D underwater game.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 is the technical SHAPE AND PLACEMENT TEMPLATE for the head armor, including the transparent eye opening. Repaint this exact isolated component in place. Preserve its canvas aspect, shape, curved rear edge, negative space and padding.
Image 2 is only the approved fish's painterly STYLE reference. Do not paint that fish, body, fins, eye or mouth.

SUBJECT / DESIGN:
A beautiful original organic bony head shield, made of three broad interlocking cranial plates protecting the fish's forehead and upper cheek. It faces RIGHT: the narrow front/snout is at RIGHT, the posterior attachment is at LEFT. Follow the template silhouette.
Make the LEFT posterior boundary deliberately flowing, asymmetric and softly scalloped with a few broad rounded overlaps. It must feel naturally grown into the skin. No straight vertical cut, rectangular panel, serrated spikes or hard sawtooth edge.
The top crown gently domes, with a smoothly tapered front snout. Two restrained CURVING sutures divide the three main plates; they should bend with the volumes and terminate naturally near the eye opening. Avoid ruler-straight seams.
A recessed dark cool-gray rim and gently modeled bony brow surround the empty eye opening. The interior of the eye opening MUST remain truly transparent: no eyeball, iris, pupil, painted black disk, eyelid or filled hole.

PAINT / STYLE:
Match the fish reference's hand-inked, softly hand-painted metroidvania art: confident tapered charcoal contours, broad quiet value planes, subtle dry-brush finish. Warm mineral bone-gray / muted ash ivory on the lit crown, cool slate-gray shadows that harmonize with the fish's skin, a few restrained pale edge highlights. Clearly bony and protective without looking like metal, polished stone, a human helmet or a carved skull.
The rear edge blends softly into the skin and has a delicate local shadow; it must not have a thick closed black sticker border. No dark C-shaped full-head ring. Keep interior detail simple enough to read when the complete fish is 45 to 90 pixels wide. No decorative motifs, repetitive scales, rivets, glowing runes, extra horns or realistic pores.

PLACEMENT / OUTPUT:
Original reference canvas is 1248 x 1104. Keep the same approximately 1.1304:1 aspect and the same transparent margin. The eye-hole center is at about 51.75% of image width and 54.59% of image height, radius about 8.94% of image width; preserve its placement and roundness.
ONE isolated head-shield overlay only, no full head, lower jaw, teeth, gill flap, body, tail, fins, surrounding fish or environment. All empty areas and the eye aperture are transparent RGBA. No background, presentation halo, shadow outside the component, border, text, numbers, measurements, grid or labels. No photorealism, 3D render, vector clipart or shiny plastic.
base: Edit this EXACT isolated painted fish head-armor component. Preserve the outer silhouette, posterior scallops, dimensions, placement, plate divisions, painterly style, all colors and transparent exterior. Make ONE technical change: FILL the circular transparent eye aperture AND its dark circular socket rim with continuous naturally modeled bone-gray armor material matching the surrounding plates. There must be NO hole, black socket, eye, pupil, iris, eyebrow or drawn circular outline remaining in that area. The game will cut and shade a correctly placed dynamic eye opening later. Continue the nearby plate planes and subtle shading coherently across the former aperture, keeping the upper sutures in their original positions and leaving the central eye area quiet. The entire armor shape is now opaque within its outer silhouette, with truly transparent background outside. No other changes. No text, labels, border, scene or new objects.
preview:
Use case: stylized-concept. A single complete PLAYER FISH with its new BONE HEAD ARMOR for EVO: Living World, a hand-painted 2D prehistoric underwater game. This is an illustrative assembly reference, not a runtime texture.
Image 1 gives the existing MAXIMUM HEAD ARMOR anatomy, head size, eye and mouth positions, and right-facing side-view orientation. Its drawing is procedural and only an anatomical reference.
Image 2 is the actual new painted armor design: use this organic warm bone-gray shield on the fish's forehead and upper cheek, with the curved scalloped posterior edge, restrained sutures and recessed eye opening. Preserve its design, do not turn it into a metal helmet or a human skull.
Image 3 gives the approved painted fish STYLE, surface finish and integrated anatomy. Use the normal fish at the TOP as the family/style reference.

Create one beautiful full right-facing side-view fish with the moderately enlarged armored head from image 1. Keep the slate-gray hand-painted body, softly pale belly, gray-ivory fins, simple forked tail and coherent anatomical joins. Only the head has bony armor. The plate's curved back edge flows into the skin near the shoulder, no straight vertical rear boundary, no separate rectangular panel. The actual eye remains a readable ivory/dark eyeball seated inside the bony aperture, and belongs to the fish; no eye painted outside the hole. Mouth nearly closed with a natural thin slit and a few small teeth. Keep the lower jaw and gill fold as gray living skin, not armored. One restrained tapered gill slit, no bright C-ring.
All volumes share the same soft overhead light, broad value shapes, dark flowing hand-inked free contour and restrained painterly brushwork. Clearly game art, not realism or 3D. No tiny repeated scales, camouflage, horns, spikes, runes, rivets, decorations or new anatomical features. It must read at 45 to 90 pixels wide.
One fish, centered, all fins and tail visible, clean truly transparent background and margin. No background water, atmosphere, halo, ground, shadow, typography, labels, guide lines, borders or additional animals.
